newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up as foreigners increase buying.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up as foreigners increase buying.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up on Friday for the third successive day as foreign investors took advantage of what they regarded as a cheap market, brokers said.
They added Monday's trade was expected to show the same trend.
Friday, the General Index rose 1.76 percent to 1,501.6 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index rose 1.5 percent to 2,065.8 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
Volume was a healthy 43.6 million soles ($17.6 million), where 57 stocks rose, 11 fell and 34 were stable in a total of 2,710 operations.

Foreign investors were absent from the market at the beginning of the week causing prices to drop. But they increasingly turned their attention to buying up cheap stocks as the week progressed, brokers said.
Once these investors brought their funds to Lima, the underlying factor that Peru's economy has healthy prospects for growth allowed this week's sudden turnaround.
The market has risen 5.1 percent since last Friday.
"Finally they (foreign investors) have realized our prices were depressed and they are taking advantage now to position themselves," said Juan Carlos Palacios of Helvetia brokerage.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 0.18 percent to 5.69 soles, in volume of 1.1 million shares.

Banco Wiese rose 2.44 percent to 4.20 soles in strong volume, accounting for 10.2 percent of the day's trade. The country's second-largest bank was attractive after the announcement earlier on Friday it signed a pact with South Korea's Export-Import Bank extending a $15 million credit to import goods from the country, brokers said.

Buenaventura saw active trade again rising 1.18 percent to 21.50 soles after news earlier in the week that the polymetal miner had won a lawsuit to exercise preemptive rights on shares in Peru's largest gold project Yanacocha, brokers said.
